Device and app version, your current settings, the last crash if there was one, and JadOO\'s own recent log. No audio, track names or personal data. Nothing is sent unless you tap Share.

More air and sparkle at the top, without touching your EQ.
Above 5 kHz the lift comes in steps: about +2.5 dB at first, up to +5.5 dB above 14.5 kHz. It makes what\'s already there brighter. It can\'t bring back detail a compressed file has already lost.

Adds weight and punch to the bass below about 260 Hz.
• **Normal** – a gentle lift • **High** – deeper and more forceful

Gives some room back to heavily compressed music.
• **Pure** – almost transparent. The limiter only catches the peaks. • **Restoration** – pushes the very quietest parts further down, so quiet and loud sit further apart.

Bass with the colour of old hardware: compression on the low end, plus a Pultec-style EQ. It copies how that gear sounds, not its circuit.
• **Drive** – squeezes the bass harder, for a denser low end • **Warmth** – adds body • **Drift** – how loosely the compression kicks in • **Pultec** – a low boost with a dip just above it

Widens the stereo image with EQ shaping alone. Vocals stay in the middle.
• **Traditional** – a little wider • **Front Stage** – brings the voice forward, like speakers in front of you • **Ultra Wide** – the most spacious

Optional. Helps JadOO find the audio session of the app that\'s playing, when Android\'s normal lookup misses it.
Grant it once from a computer:
**adb shell pm grant com.jadoo.amp android.permission.DUMP**

A warm valve-amp colour, good for thin or clinical-sounding tracks. It\'s tone only: a soft bass bloom and a gentler top end. Real tube saturation isn\'t possible on Android, so this is the closest it gets.

Makes your phone\'s small speaker sound fuller. It can\'t reach real sub-bass, so it lifts the notes just above that, where the speaker can keep up.
Only appears when audio plays through the phone speaker.

Adds presence and clarity between 2 and 8 kHz, where voices and attacks live.
It\'s a gentle lift, not new harmonics. Push it too far on bright tracks and it can turn harsh. Works on every output.

Up to 16 filters on top of the graphic EQ.
The engine runs them through the same 15 bands as the graphic EQ, so narrow filters come out wider than you set them. The curve on the home screen shows what\'s really applied.

Two styles for SBC Bluetooth. Use whichever sounds better to you.
• **Classic** – brighter and more open • **New** – shapes the signal before the codec, for smoother cymbals and less watery hiss
SBC shares out its bits by loudness and re-shares them every 3 ms. New trims the very top, where bits are expensive and hard to hear, and steadies the highs so they don\'t break up.
SBC only. If your headphones support LDAC, LHDC or aptX HD, use one of those instead.

Quiet music loses bass and treble, because that\'s how ears work. This adds them back as you turn down, so the balance stays the same.
## Reference level How loud your gear gets at full volume. Set it by ear, with a track you know.
## Amount How much correction to apply. Turn it down if full strength is too much.

Gives each app its own settings, switched on as soon as it starts playing. For example, a speech lift for podcasts and the full curve for music.
Saved per app and per output.

Boosts need room above loud songs, or they clip.
## On (recommended) On wired and speaker, the input is turned down just enough that the song stays as loud as it is with effects off. On Bluetooth, boosts only ease off on the loudest moments, so nothing is turned down.
## Keep full loudness Wired, DAC and speaker only. Effects no longer lower the volume at full volume, but loud songs can clip. Bluetooth isn\'t affected.
## Off No protection. Loud songs can clip with several boosts on. Only useful for comparing with older versions.
